nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian Process Regression (non-parametric) from PCNToolkit used to compute normative trajectories as a function of age.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Utilising the non-  parametric Gaussian Process Regression model to derive the normative trajectories

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled three quantitative MRI (qMRI) parameters: R1 (longitudinal relaxation rate), R2* (apparent transverse relaxation rate), and magnetic susceptibility (χ) in basal ganglia subcortical nuclei. Additionally, tissue volumes of subcortical ROIs were extracted and normalized by intracranial brain volume. The qMRI parameters R1, R2*, and χ do not map directly to the provided minor categories but are quantitative imaging-derived phenotypes related to tissue microstructure (myelination and iron deposition).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Quantitative MRI parameters, including the longitudinal relaxation rate R1, apparent transverse relaxation rate R2*, and tissue magnetic susceptibility χ, are gaining prominence as surrogate biomarkers for myelin and iron concentrations. ... The tissue volumes of all subcortical ROIs were also extracted and normalised by the intracranial brain volume.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The General Linear Model design matrix comprised four regressors: Age (linear term), Age² (quadratic term to capture inverted U-shaped effects observed in R1 data), Sex, and Hemisphere (left/right). Data were corrected for sex-specific and inter-hemispherical effects based on GLM results before Gaussian Process Regression analysis.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The design matrix comprised four regressors: Age, Age², Sex, and (left-/right-) Hemisphere... The utility of Age² as a regressor is to consider the inverted U-shaped effect observed in our R1 data which were also shown previously.
